 Alex Kwong testifies in Abby Choi murder trial over car argument
 By Erwin Wong - 12:27PM Fri November 20, 2026 722 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 Pinterest 
 Telegram 
 Alex Kwong 
 20th November 2026 – (Hong Kong) Giving evidence in his own defence at the High Court in Hong Kong, former husband and third defendant Alex Kwong Kong-chi testified about his final car journey with socialite Abby Choi before the alleged fatal incident. He told the court that Choi was in the seven-seater vehicle when he got in and was messaging her mother-in-law on WeChat or WhatsApp while discussing family matters.
 According to Alex Kwong, Choi complained during the drive that her mother, Cheung Yin-fa, owed money again from gambling debts, saying she had to pay HK$100,000 a month in principal and HK$80,000 in interest and felt under heavy pressure. He said he tried to comfort her by telling her not to worry too much because it was not a huge sum and there was no way around it, while noting that the two of them spoke in a mix of Hainanese and Cantonese.
 Alex Kwong further testified that Choi spoke about buying clothes for her mother-in-law and looking at properties in Tuen Mun, asking him to check out developments at Gold Coast and Mount Regency when he had time. Later in the journey, their conversation turned to Choi being unable to reach her children on the first day of the Lunar New Year after Kwong Kau had taken them out, with Kwong Kau reportedly warning that he would not cooperate on other matters if prevented from seeing his grandchildren.
 The defendant told the jury that Choi became furious upon hearing this and demanded that he speak with Kwong Kau, prompting him to reply that he could not intervene when it involved the children. He alleged that Choi swore at him, criticised Kwong Kau, and insisted on meeting Kwong Kau immediately to clear things up, leading older brother and first defendant Anthony Kwong Kong-kit to locate Kwong Kau in Tai Po and drive to a car park in Tai Mei Tuk.
 Alex Kwong said Choi remained angry when they reached the Tai Mei Tuk car park, where Kwong Kau had already stepped out of his own vehicle and handed Alex Kwong a document, saying it had been sorted out before getting into the seven-seater with Choi. He testified that after he and Anthony Kwong finished smoking outside and reopened the seven-seater door, Choi was lying on the floor while Kwong Kau sat inside.
 Kwong Kau reportedly told them not to talk yet and to go back to the village house first before returning to his own car, according to Alex Kwong’s testimony. Alex Kwong added that he got into the vehicle to check on Choi, saw blood on the right side of her head, moved her hand, called out to her, and checked whether she had a heartbeat or was breathing, while Kwong Kau wiped away tears in court and Anthony Kwong took notes with his head bowed.
 Three defendants, aged 35-year-old driver Anthony Kwong Kong-kit, 69-year-old retiree Kwong Kau, and 32-year-old unemployed Alex Kwong Kong-chi, are charged with murdering Abby Choi in Hong Kong on 21st February 2023 and preventing the lawful burial of her body between 21st February 2023 and 23rd February 2023. The judge previously informed the jury that all three defendants have pleaded not guilty to murder while admitting one count of preventing the lawful burial of a body.
